verses.text: This is a message, the word of the LORD to Israel through Malachi.
"I have loved you," says the LORD. But you ask, "How have you loved us?" "Wasn't Esau Jacob's brother?" says the LORD. "Yet I loved Jacob,
but I rejected Esau. I turned his mountains into a wasteland and left his land to the jackals of the desert."

Edom may say, "We have been crushed, but we will rebuild the ruins." But this is what the LORD of Armies says: "They may build, but I will tear down. People will call them the Wicked Land, a people the LORD is angry with forever.
You will see it with your own eyes and say, 'Great is the LORD — even beyond the borders of Israel!'

"A son honors his father, and a servant honors his master. If I am a father, where is the honor due me? If I am a master, where is the respect due me?" says the LORD of Armies to you priests who show contempt for my name. "But you ask, 'How have we shown contempt for your name?'
By offering unclean food on my altar. But you ask, 'How have we made you unclean?' By saying that the LORD's table is not worth anything.

When you bring blind animals for sacrifice, isn't that wrong? When you bring injured or sick animals, isn't that wrong? Try offering them to your governor! Would he be pleased with you? Would he accept you?" says the LORD of Armies.
"Now plead with God to be kind to us. With offerings like these from your hands, will he accept any of you?" says the LORD of Armies.

"I wish one of you would shut the temple doors, so that you would not light useless fires on my altar! I am not pleased with you," says the LORD of Armies, "and I will not accept any offering from your hands.

My name will be great among the nations, from where the sun rises to where it sets. In every place incense and pure offerings will be brought to my name, because my name will be great among the nations," says the LORD of Armies.
"But you treat it as unclean when you say, 'The LORD's table is unclean, and the food on it is not worth anything.'

And you say, 'What a burden!' and you sniff at it with contempt," says the LORD of Armies. "When you bring injured, lame, or sick animals and offer them as sacrifices, should I accept them from your hands?" says the LORD.

"Cursed is the cheat who has an acceptable male animal in his flock and vows to give it, but then sacrifices a damaged animal to the Lord. For I am a great King," says the LORD of Armies, "and my name is to be feared among the nations."
